output.name: Solva
output.myth: When Aun cut the string he was still wearing his good sleeve, the one his mother cut from her own wedding cloth. Tavo the Gale came down the cliffs that night, caught the sleeve on a gull-stake and tore it to the elbow, laughing. Halun the Full Beak, who fished the cold water under the cliffs, saw it with her beak full and her chicks waiting, and she said nothing. Aun could not climb back with one arm of cloth open to the wind, so he sat and wept. Ennu the Kite-Wright came from the west, under the Ferry Sail being loaded for spring, with a scrap of Sil's old sail, and sewed a patch over the torn place. The patch did not match. Ennu said that was the point. Hesk counted the stitches, and there were nine hundred and six, and she never lets anyone forget it. The Torn Sleeve hangs over the Reach still, ragged at the wrist where the Gale got his fingers in. If you are mending something that will not match, do not unpick it. A mended thing can still hold wind.
output.finding: Find Halun, the Full Beak, and Solva lies about one fist (9°) to its west, in the northern Windward Reach.
